title: Graph Valid Tree / Redundant Connection Detection
contract: Return whether undirected edges form one tree on n ≥ 1 vertices. Self-loops and duplicate edges invalidate a tree.
brute: if(edges.length!=n-1)return false;boolean[][] reach=new boolean[n][n];for(int i=0;i<n;i++)reach[i][i]=true;for(int[] edge:edges){reach[edge[0]][edge[1]]=true;reach[edge[1]][edge[0]]=true;}for(int k=0;k<n;k++){for(int i=0;i<n;i++)for(int j=0;j<n;j++)reach[i][j]|=reach[i][k]&&reach[k][j];emit("Compute reachability","via",k);}for(int i=0;i<n;i++)if(!reach[0][i])return false;return true;
optimal: if(edges.length!=n-1)return false;int[] parent=new int[n],size=new int[n];for(int i=0;i<n;i++){parent[i]=i;size[i]=1;}for(int[] edge:edges){int a=find(parent,edge[0]),b=find(parent,edge[1]);emit("An edge within one component would close a cycle","edge",edge,"roots",new int[]{a,b});if(a==b)return false;if(size[a]<size[b]){int t=a;a=b;b=t;}parent[b]=a;size[a]+=size[b];}return true;
reasoning: A graph on n vertices with n−1 edges is a tree exactly when it is connected; the baseline computes reachability.
DSU rejects an edge joining two vertices already in the same component.
With n−1 successful unions, all vertices are connected automatically. The rejected edge is also the core signal in redundant-connection problems, although this lab returns a boolean.
